# opc-probe (phase-0 spike plugin)

Minimal host plugin for the opc-workbench phase-0 spike. It exists to produce
machine-checkable evidence for three claims; it is not product code and carries
no business logic.

## What it proves

1. **Own-profile bundle loading.** The `opc-workbench` profile (derived from
   the shipped `web` template) lists `@local/opc-probe` in
   `dsh.profile.bundles`; this package's `cordis.patch.yml` carries the
   `insert` entry that mounts it into the cordis tree with its config. The DSH
   kernel is not modified.
2. **Runtime activation.** `apply(ctx, config)` writes
   `../evidence/plugin-active-marker.json` and registers two routes on the
   host `webServer` (bound to 127.0.0.1 by the profile's webserver row).
3. **AgentRuntime target surface.** `POST /opc-probe/v1/run` drives the
   in-process `sessionController` through the full chain
   `create -> prompt -> follow -> cancel` and returns the ordered
   protocol-layer event stream as evidence. LLM output quality is never part
   of the verdict.

## Version pinning

`package.json` declares `engines.dsh: 0.2.2-rc.1` (the locked runtime, see
`docs/decisions/0001-dsh-integration.md`). The app-boot compatibility gate
evaluates this range at load; a mismatch fails explicitly instead of loading
a plugin built against a different harness.

## Routes

- `GET /opc-probe/v1/health` - liveness of the plugin inside the host.
- `POST /opc-probe/v1/run` - body `{"text": "...", "collectMillis": 90000,
  "settleMillis": 10000}` (all optional). Returns
  `{ok, result:{sessionId, cancel, follow:{...}, afterCancelFrames, ...}}`.

Both routes enforce the same-origin / loopback guard and JSON-only writes,
following the shipped company-console precedent: plugin routes bypass the host
token gate, so the plugin refuses cross-site and cross-origin callers itself.

## Files

- `index.js` - plugin entry (`name`, `inject`, `apply`).
- `cordis.patch.yml` - bundle patch layer with the insert entry.
- `package.json` - manifest with the `engines.dsh` pin.
